title: Krishna Recognizes the Disguised Pandavas at Draupadi's Svayamvara
one_line_summary: At Draupadi's svayamvara, Krishna, seated among the Yadava chiefs, recognizes the five Pandavas disguised as Brahmins and tells Balarama who each of them is.
source_excerpt: And Halayudha (Valadeva) and Janardana (Krishna) and the chief of the Vrishni, Andhaka, and Yadava tribes who obeyed the leadership of Krishna were also there, viewing the scene. And beholding those elephants in rut--the five (Pandavas)--attracted towards Draupadi like mighty elephants towards a lake overgrown with lotuses, or like fire covered with ashes, Krishna the foremost of Yadu heroes began to reflect. And he said unto Rama (Valadeva), 'That is Yudhishthira; that is Bhima with Jishnu (Arjuna); and those are the twin heroes.'

title: Krishna Rejoices as Arjuna Wins Draupadi
one_line_summary: Seeing Arjuna string the stiff bow and shoot the mark, Krishna is filled with joy and approaches the disguised Pandava with a white robe and a garland of flowers.
source_excerpt: And Krishna beholding the mark shot and beholding Partha also like unto Indra himself, who had shot the mark, was filled with joy, and approached the son of Kunti with a white robe and a garland of flowers.

title: Krishna Names Each Pandava to Balarama
one_line_summary: After Bhima uproots a tree and Arjuna readies his bow against the angry kings, Krishna tells Balarama who each Pandava is, and Balarama rejoices that their aunt Kunti and her sons escaped the house of lac.
source_excerpt: And beholding those feats of both Jishnu and his brother, Damodara (Krishna) of superhuman intelligence and inconceivable feats, addressing his brother, Halayudha (Valadeva) of fierce energy, said, 'That hero there, of tread like that of a mighty lion, who draweth the large bow in his hand four full cubits in length, is Arjuna! ... And that other hero who having speedily torn up the tree hath suddenly become ready to drive off the monarchs is Vrikodara! ... I heard that the sons of Pandu along with their mother Pritha had all escaped from the conflagration of the house of lac.' Then Halayudha ... said with great satisfaction, 'O, I am happy to hear ... that our father's sister Pritha with the foremost of the Kaurava princes have all escaped (from death)!'

title: Krishna Stops the Angry Kings from Attacking the Pandavas
one_line_summary: When the insulted kings rush to attack Drupada and the Pandavas, Krishna declares that Draupadi has been justly won and persuades the monarchs to abandon the fight.
source_excerpt: And Krishna, having beheld that feat of Bhima, believed them both to be the son of Kunti. And gently addressing the assembled monarchs, saying, 'This maiden hath been justly acquired (by the Brahmana),' he induced them to abandon the fight. Accomplished in battle, those monarchs then desisted from the fight.

title: Krishna and Balarama Meet the Pandavas at the Potter's House
one_line_summary: Suspecting the Pandavas to be alive, Krishna and Balarama come to the potter's house, touch Yudhishthira's and Kunti's feet, and warn the disguised brothers to keep hidden.
source_excerpt: The hero of the Vrishni race (Krishna suspecting the five persons he had seen at the Swayamvara to be none else than the heroes of the Kuru race), came accompanied by the son of Rohini (Valadeva), to the house of the potter ... Then Vasudeva approaching that foremost of virtuous men--the son of Kunti--and touching the feet of that prince of the Ajamida race, said, 'I am Krishna.' ... And Ajatasatru ... asked, 'How, O Vasudeva, hast thou been able to trace us, as we are living in disguise?' And Vasudeva, smilingly answered, 'O king, fire, even if it is covered, can be known. ... And lest any of the monarchs recognise ye, let us return to our tent.'

title: Krishna Sends Lavish Wedding Gifts to the Pandavas
one_line_summary: After the Pandavas' marriage to Draupadi, Krishna sends them gold ornaments, costly robes, gems, elephants, horses, and crores of gold coins, which Yudhishthira accepts with joy.
source_excerpt: After the sons of Pandu had been married, Hari (Krishna) sent unto them (as presents) various gold ornaments set with pearls and black gems (lapis lazuli). And Madhava (Krishna) also sent unto them costly robes manufactured in various countries ... He also sent them vessels by hundreds, set with gems and diamonds. ... The slayer of Madhu, of immeasurable soul, also sent them coins of pure gold by crores upon crores in separate heaps. And Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all those presents with great joy.

title: Krishna Embraces Arjuna at Prabhasa and Hosts Him at Dwaraka
one_line_summary: During Arjuna's forest exile, Krishna learns of his arrival at Prabhasa and goes to meet him; the two friends, Nara and Narayana of old, embrace and Krishna hosts Arjuna at Dwaraka for many days.
source_excerpt: Vibhatsu reached the sacred spot called Prabhasa. When the invisible Arjuna arrived at that sacred and delightful region, the slayer of Madhu (Krishna) heard of it. Madhava soon went there to see his friend, the son of Kunti. Krishna and Arjuna met together and embracing each other enquired after each other's welfare. Those dear friends, who were none else than the Rishis Nara and Narayana of old, sat down. ... he took up his abode there with Krishna for many days.

title: Krishna Counsels Arjuna to Abduct Subhadra
one_line_summary: At the Raivataka festival, Krishna notices Arjuna's love for his sister Subhadra and advises him to carry her away by force, the celebrated Kshatriya form of marriage.
source_excerpt: Krishna, observing Partha contemplate her with absorbed attention, said with a smile, 'How is this? Can the heart of one that rangeth the woods be agitated by the god of desire? This is my sister, O Partha ... Tell me if thy heart is fixed upon her, for I shall then speak to my father myself.' ... Vasudeva answered, 'O bull amongst men, self-choice hath been ordained for the marriage of Kshatriyas. But that is doubtful (in its consequences) ... In the case of Kshatriyas that are brave, a forcible abduction for purposes of marriage is applauded, as the learned have said. Therefore O Arjuna, carry away this my beautiful sister by force, for who knows what she may do at a self-choice.'
variant_notes: Section 221 calls the maiden 'Bhadra' and 'the daughter of Vasudeva'; she is the Subhadra of later sections.

title: Krishna Defends Arjuna's Abduction of Subhadra Before the Yadavas
one_line_summary: When the enraged Yadava warriors arm to punish Arjuna, Krishna tells them the alliance is honourable and directs them to bring Arjuna back by conciliation; Subhadra and Arjuna are then married.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva uttered these words pregnant with deep import and consistent with true morality. Gudakesa (the conqueror of sleep or he of the curly hair), by what he hath done, hath not insulted our family. He hath without doubt, rather enhanced our respect. ... I think Arjuna, seeing these faults in all the other methods took the maiden away by force, according to the ordinance. This alliance is very proper. ... go ye cheerfully after Dhananjaya and by conciliation stop him and bring him back. ... Hearing, O monarch, those words of Vasudeva, they did as he directed. Stopped by them, Arjuna returned to Dwaraka and was united in marriage with Subhadra.
variant_notes: The Yadavas' armament and Balarama's wrath occupy section 222; Krishna's pacifying speech is in section 223.

title: Krishna Comes to Indraprastha Bearing Nuptial Gifts
one_line_summary: Hearing that Arjuna has reached Indraprastha with Subhadra, Krishna arrives with the Yadava host and presents the Pandavas with cars, cows, mares, mules, and damsels as nuptial gifts.
source_excerpt: When that scorcher of foes, viz., Kesava of pure soul ... heard that the foremost of the Pandavas, viz., Arjuna, had reached his own excellent city of Indraprastha, he came thither accompanied by Rama and the other heroes ... bringing with them many nuptial presents. ... Krishna gave unto the Pandavas a thousand cars of gold furnished with rows of bells ... He also gave unto them ten thousand cows belonging to the country of Mathura ... Well-pleased, Janardana also gave them a thousand mares with gold harnesses and of colour white as the beams of the moon.

title: Krishna Performs the Birth Rites of Abhimanyu
one_line_summary: Krishna stays on at Indraprastha with Arjuna, and when Subhadra bears Abhimanyu, Krishna performs the infant's birth rites; the child grows dear to him.
source_excerpt: the high-souled Vasudeva remained there with Arjuna in the delightful city of Indraprastha. ... Then Subhadra, the favourite sister of Kesava, gave birth to an illustrious son ... And the son that Subhadra brought forth ... came to be called Abhimanyu. ... Upon his birth, Krishna performed the usual rites of infancy. The child began to grow up like the Moon of the bright fortnight.

title: Krishna and Arjuna Sport on the Yamuna and Receive a Mysterious Brahmana
one_line_summary: In summer Krishna and Arjuna go with friends to sport on the banks of the Yamuna, where a radiant Brahmana suddenly approaches the seated heroes.
source_excerpt: After a few days, Vibhatsu, addressing Krishna, said, 'The summer days have set in, O Krishna! Therefore, let us go to the banks of the Yamuna. ...' Thereupon Vasudeva said, 'O son of Kunti, this is also my wish. ...' ... Unto Vasudeva and Dhananjaya happily sitting there like the Aswins in heaven, a certain Brahmana came. ... Beholding that foremost of Brahmanas blazing with splendour approach towards them both Arjuna and Vasudeva, hastily rising from their seats, stood, waiting (for his commands).
notes: Opening of the Khandava-daha episode; the actual burning lies beyond this section range.

title: Agni, in Brahman Disguise, Seeks Krishna and Arjuna's Help to Burn Khandava
one_line_summary: The Brahmana reveals himself as Agni and asks Krishna and Arjuna to shield him from Indra's rains so he can consume the Khandava forest.
source_excerpt: Then that Brahmana addressed Arjuna and Vasudeva of the Satwata race, saying, 'Ye who are now staying so near unto Khandava are the two foremost of heroes on earth. I am a voracious Brahmana that always eateth much. ... I solicit you to gratify me by giving me sufficient food.' ... The illustrious Brahmana, thus replied to, said ... 'I do not desire to eat ordinary food. Know that I am Agni! ... This forest of Khandava is always protected by Indra. ... I pray you to prevent those showers from descending and any of the creatures from escaping, when I begin to consume this forest!'
variant_notes: The remainder of section 225 (the Swetaki-sacrifice backstory explaining Agni's surfeit) is narrated as a Puranic flashback and contains no further Krishna action.
notes: Setup of the Khandava-daha; the burning itself and Krishna's role against Indra continue in later sections not in this bundle.
